title: Introduction to GitHub
overview: GitHub is a cloud-based platform that hosts Git repositories and helps developers collaborate on projects.

example.content:

title: Creating a GitHub Repository
overview: A GitHub repository stores project code online and provides collaboration features.

example.content:
GitHub Account
 ↓

title: Connecting Local Repository with GitHub
overview: A local Git repository can be connected to GitHub using a remote repository URL.

title: Git Push Command
overview: The git push command uploads local commits to a remote GitHub repository.

title: Git Pull Command
overview: The git pull command downloads the latest changes from a remote repository.

title: Fork and Clone
overview: Fork creates a personal copy of a repository, while clone downloads a repository to your local machine.

title: Pull Requests
overview: Pull requests allow developers to propose changes and review code before merging into the main branch.
